summary: Verified bug fix: mobile navbar 'Network' link now navigates to /network page (same as desktop) instead of scrolling to homepage #network anchor. Ran 8 Playwright flows covering the fix + all specified regressions on both viewports (390x844 mobile, 1440x900 desktop). All 8 passed.

(Optional) Add position:relative on the Framer Motion scroll container to silence warning.
critical_code_review_comments: Mobile menu markup is hardcoded in Navbar.jsx (lines ~170-235) and duplicates NAV_LINKS from /app/frontend/src/data/company.js. This duplication is exactly what caused the original bug (desktop used NAV_LINKS with '/network', mobile had hardcoded '/#network'). Recommend driving the mobile menu off NAV_LINKS as single source of truth to prevent recurrence.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix verified end-to-end on preview URL. Mobile 'Network' lands on /network with H1 'Infrastructure connecting Southeast Asia.' and breadcrumb Home / Network. Desktop Network, Services dropdown->Dark Fiber, footer Network Coverage, and intentional anchor behavior for mobile Home/Solutions/About all still work. No backend testing done (frontend-only request).
rca of the issue: Root cause: Navbar.jsx hardcoded the mobile 'Network' link as to='/#network' (a homepage hash anchor), while the desktop navbar derived links from NAV_LINKS in data/company.js where Network -> '/network'. ScrollManager interpreted '/#network' as scroll-to-anchor on homepage, so mobile users were scrolled to the 'OUR NETWORK' preview section on '/' instead of being routed to the dedicated /network page. Fix: changed mobile link to to='/network' (Navbar.jsx line ~174). Verified: URL path becomes /network, dedicated page H1 'Infrastructure connecting Southeast Asia.' and 'NETWORK FOOTPRINT' country tabs render. Mitigation to prevent future drift: drive mobile menu from the same NAV_LINKS source used by desktop.
